title: Diffusion Forward Process
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Forward diffusion gradually adds Gaussian noise until data is nearly pure noise.
long: Destroy structure by noise. Closed form at any timestep.
proof: Combine Gaussian steps by variance additivity.

title: Diffusion Models Learn to Denoise
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Reversing the noising process with a learned denoiser yields samples from the data distribution.
long: Generation is iterative denoising. Training can predict added noise.
proof: Fit reverse conditionals using forward posteriors.

title: Denoising Estimates the Score
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Predicting noise at a corrupted point is equivalent to estimating the gradient of the log density of the smoothed data.
long: Denoisers estimate scores. Follows from Gaussian convolution identities.

title: Message Passing in GNNs
subject: Neural Networks
statement: GNNs update node representations by aggregating information from neighbours.
long: Nodes exchange messages. Layers propagate multiple hops.

title: Over Smoothing in Deep GNNs
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Many message passing layers can make node representations converge and become indistinguishable.
long: Too many layers blur identities. Empirical with theoretical analyses.

title: Attention Is Permutation Equivariant
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Self attention without positional encodings treats tokens as a set.
long: No built in order. Explains need for positional encodings.

title: Xavier Initialization
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Initial weights scaled by fan in and fan out help keep activation variances stable.
long: Scale initialization by width. Variance preservation heuristic.

title: He Initialization
subject: Neural Networks
statement: For ReLU nets variance two over fan in accounts for half the activations being zeroed.
long: ReLU needs larger variance. Derived from variance preservation.

title: Transfer Learning
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Features learned on a large source task can be reused for a related target task.
long: Reuse learned representations. Works when tasks share structure empirically.

title: Fine Tuning
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Fine tuning continues training a pretrained model on task data with a lower learning rate.
long: Adapt a pretrained net. Lower rates preserve features.
proof: Run gradient steps on target data.

title: Neural Tangent Kernel
subject: Neural Networks
statement: In the infinite width limit network training follows kernel gradient descent with the neural tangent kernel.
short: Wide nets behave like kernel machines.
long: Wide nets behave like kernel machines. Holds under specific scaling limits.
proof: Take the width limit of gradient flow.

title: Gradient Descent
subject: Optimization
statement: Gradient descent iteratively moves in the negative gradient direction.
long: Step downhill. Step size controls speed and stability.
proof: Apply the first order descent direction.

title: Negative Gradient Is Steepest Descent
subject: Optimization
statement: The negative gradient is the steepest descent direction in Euclidean norm.
long: Steepest local decrease. Cauchy Schwarz gives the result.
proof: Minimize the linear approximation over the unit ball.

title: Smooth Convex Convergence of Gradient Descent
subject: Optimization
statement: For convex L smooth functions with step one over L gradient descent reduces the gap at rate one over t.
long: Smooth convex descent is sublinear. Use the descent lemma and convexity.

title: Strong Convexity Gives Linear Convergence
subject: Optimization
statement: For strongly convex smooth functions gradient descent with step one over L converges linearly.
long: Curvature gives exponential convergence. Contract distance to the optimum.
consequence: Faster rates for well conditioned problems.

title: Convex Function Definition
subject: Optimization
statement: A function is convex when it lies below the chord between any two points.
long: Function below its chords. Differentiable convexity equals the gradient inequality.

title: Strong Convexity Definition
subject: Optimization
statement: Strong convexity adds a positive quadratic lower bound to convexity.
long: Convexity plus curvature. It implies a unique minimizer.
proof: Add a quadratic to a convex function.

title: L Smoothness Definition
subject: Optimization
statement: L smoothness means the gradient is L Lipschitz.
long: Gradients cannot change too quickly. It yields the descent lemma.

title: Stochastic Gradient Descent
subject: Optimization
statement: SGD updates using an unbiased gradient estimate from one or a few samples.
long: Noisy gradient steps. Noise falls with mini batch size.
proof: Sample an index and compute its gradient.

title: Stochastic Gradient Is Unbiased
subject: Optimization
statement: Uniform index sampling makes the stochastic gradient equal the full gradient in expectation.
long: Gradient noise has zero mean. Sample average is unbiased.

title: Robbins Monro Step Size Conditions
subject: Optimization
statement: For convex stochastic objectives step sizes with divergent sum and square summable values give convergence.
short: Shrink steps but not too fast.
long: Shrink steps but not too fast. Bound accumulated variance.

title: Momentum
subject: Optimization
statement: Momentum accumulates an exponentially decaying average of past gradients.
long: Keep moving in consistent directions. Damps oscillation in narrow valleys.

title: Nesterov Accelerated Gradient
subject: Optimization
statement: Nesterov momentum evaluates the gradient at a look ahead point.
long: Look before stepping. Optimal for smooth convex functions.

title: Accelerated Rate Is Optimal
subject: Optimization
statement: No first order method beats one over t squared for smooth convex functions in the black box model.
short: The accelerated rate cannot improve generally.
long: The accelerated rate cannot improve generally. Construct hard high dimensional quadratics.

title: Adam Optimizer
subject: Optimization
statement: Adam maintains decaying averages of gradients and squared gradients and normalizes each coordinate.
long: Adaptive per parameter step sizes. Combines momentum with RMS scaling.
